Let  
\[
a=\sin^2 x,\quad b=\cos^2 x,\quad c=\sin x\cos x.
\]
Set \(t=\tan x\), where \(0<t<\infty\). Then
\[
a=\frac{t^2}{1+t^2},\quad b=\frac{1}{1+t^2},\quad c=\frac{t}{1+t^2}.
\]

For these to be side lengths of a triangle, the only nontrivial conditions are
\[
a+c>b \quad\text{and}\quad b+c>a.
\]
Multiplying by \(1+t^2>0\), these become
\[
t^2+t>1 \quad\Rightarrow\quad t>\frac{\sqrt5-1}{2}=\frac1\phi
\]
and
\[
1+t>t^2 \quad\Rightarrow\quad t<\frac{1+\sqrt5}{2}=\phi.
\]
So a triangle is formed exactly when
\[
\frac1\phi<t<\phi.
\]

Thus non-triangle occurs for
\[
0<t\le \frac1\phi \quad\text{or}\quad t\ge \phi.
\]
In degrees, the total measure of non-triangle \(x\)-values is
\[
\arctan\left(\frac1\phi\right)+\left(90^\circ-\arctan\phi\right).
\]
Since \(\frac1\phi\cdot\phi=1\), we have
\[
\arctan\left(\frac1\phi\right)+\arctan\phi=90^\circ,
\]
so the total is
\[
2\arctan\left(\frac1\phi\right).
\]
Now let \(\alpha=\frac1\phi\). Since \(\alpha^2+\alpha=1\),
\[
\tan(2\arctan\alpha)=\frac{2\alpha}{1-\alpha^2}=\frac{2\alpha}{\alpha}=2.
\]
Hence
\[
2\arctan\left(\frac1\phi\right)=\arctan 2
\]
in degrees.

The probability is therefore
\[
p=\frac{\arctan 2\text{ in degrees}}{90}.
\]
So \(m=2\), \(n=90\), and
\[
m+n=92.
\]

The answer is 92.
